relatedSnapshot.title: Workspace email and conferencing settings affect other workspaces
relatedSnapshot.description:
Workspace settings are not isolated between workspaces.

### Problem

Changing email/calendar or conferencing settings in one workspace affects other workspaces. These settings appear under the **Personal** section of the settings page rather than the **Workspace** section.

### Current Behavior

* Email and conferencing configuration changed in one workspace also changes in another workspace.
* The controls for these settings are located under the Personal section, which may be causing them to apply across workspaces.

### Expected Behavior

* Each workspace should have independent settings.
* Updating email/calendar or conferencing configuration in one workspace should not impact any other workspace.
* Workspace-specific configuration should live under the Workspace section of settings.

A screen recording of the issue is available in Jam: screen recording.

relatedSnapshot.title: Workspace email and calendar bleed across workspaces
relatedSnapshot.description:

The issue also appears to affect booking and handler behavior. Meetings can route to the client's email/calendar while showing the user's name, and the client cannot be selected as a call handler in their own workspace even after being added as an owner and connecting their calendar.

The customer shared that the client workspace dashboard can still show the user's workspace context, and they are unable to keep the two workspaces separated for campaign bookings.

relatedSnapshot.title: Email & calendar connections are shared across all workspaces
relatedSnapshot.description:
Email and calendar connections behave as account-level rather than workspace-scoped, causing the same email to appear in all workspaces a user can access.

Observed behavior:

* User connects their own email/calendar in their personal workspace under Settings → Email & Calendar
* After switching to a client workspace, the same email/calendar automatically appears there without any explicit connection
* Deleting the email connection from the client workspace also deletes it from the user’s own workspace

Impact/expectation:

* User expects separate email connections per workspace (own workspace vs client workspace) so that each workspace only uses the inboxes for that specific business
* Current behavior makes it impossible to fully isolate operator vs client email/calendar per workspace and is confusing from a UX perspective

Context from this conversation:

* User is managing both their own workspace and a client workspace ("Name 100 and Name 2 (Name 3)")
* They want their email/calendar connected only in their own workspace and their client’s email/calendar connected only in the client workspace, but the platform currently treats the connection as global.

Please investigate whether email/calendar connections can be scoped per workspace instead of at the account level, or otherwise adjust behavior/UX so that workspace‑specific email connections are possible or clearly communicated.

relatedSnapshot.title: Let a rep turn email sync on per workspace so one inbox works in several CRMs
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A rep who belongs to more than one CRM workspace can choose, from Email & Calendar settings, which of those workspaces their connected Gmail or Outlook inbox syncs into. Today an inbox can only ever sync into one workspace at a time, and nothing in settings shows or controls which one.

Raised by James on 16 September as the next step after the inbox-follows-the-rep fix.

## Problem

Since the workspace lock on connected inboxes shipped on 04 September, every inbox has exactly one active workspace record. Let a rep's inbox follow them to the workspace they send from unblocked sending: the first send from a workspace moves the inbox there. But sync moves with it. A rep who works in two CRMs, for example their own agency workspace and a client's, gets email history and new mail in only the workspace they last sent from, and the other one silently stops syncing. There is no way to say "sync this inbox into both", and the Email & Calendar settings page lists inboxes by person with no workspace information at all.

## Proposed fix

In Email & Calendar settings, each connected inbox shows the workspaces the rep belongs to with an "Email sync" switch per workspace. Turning it on for a workspace starts importing recent history and keeping new mail flowing into that workspace. Turning it off stops sync there and keeps the CRM history already imported. An inbox can be on in several workspaces at once, and sending from any of them keeps working as it does today.

## What's included

Included: the per-workspace sync switch in Email & Calendar settings for Gmail and Outlook inboxes; allowing one inbox to have an active sync record in more than one workspace; starting the recent-history import when a workspace is switched on; stopping sync cleanly when it is switched off; and keeping the automatic bind-on-send behavior from Let a rep's inbox follow them to the workspace they send from working alongside it.

Excluded: calendar sync, which stays as it is today; shared mailboxes and aliases, which stay in Inbox sync follow-ups; and any change to which emails get linked to which contact, which is owned by Link synced emails to CRM records we already know.

Builds on the workspace record from Record which workspace each connected mailbox belongs to and the sync health states from Show Gmail sync health and finish disconnect cleanup, which should land first so the settings page already has a per-inbox sync section to extend.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Tickets explicitly grouped as parallel may start together when there is capacity, but they still keep the priority order below. Waves show the earliest dependency unlock, not a barrier: start a later-wave ticket as soon as its own blockers are complete.

### Wave 1: can start now

1. Let one connected mailbox hold an active binding in more than one workspace: makes it possible, underneath, for a mailbox to hold an active binding in more than one workspace, with no visible change yet.

### Wave 2: starts once priority 1 completes

Parallel: Show a per-workspace Email sync switch in Email & Calendar settings and Fan Gmail live sync out to every workspace an inbox is switched on in.

2. Show a per-workspace Email sync switch in Email & Calendar settings: blocked by Let one connected mailbox hold an active binding in more than one workspace. Delivers the settings switch reps actually see and use.
3. Fan Gmail live sync out to every workspace an inbox is switched on in: blocked by Let one connected mailbox hold an active binding in more than one workspace. Delivers ongoing Gmail mail actually arriving in every switched-on workspace, not just a one-time import.

Cross-wave overlap: none verified. Both priority 2 and priority 3 need priority 1's workspace-scoped binding helpers before either can start, but neither blocks the other.

## How it should work

Each inbox keeps one sync record per workspace instead of one in total. Switching a workspace on creates or reactivates its record and kicks off the same recent-history import a fresh connect does. Switching it off deactivates that record, stops background sync for that workspace, and leaves imported history in place. Bind-on-send keeps its current behavior for a workspace that is switched off: sending from there binds the inbox and, from then on, that workspace counts as switched on. Disconnecting the inbox switches every workspace off at once, as today. Background sync, webhooks and calendar never turn a workspace on by themselves.

## Who can do what

Only the inbox owner can see or change the switches for their own inbox, and only for workspaces they are currently a member of. Leaving a workspace switches it off. Workspace admins cannot turn another person's inbox on or off.

## What the user sees

Under Email & Calendar, each connected inbox lists the rep's workspaces with a switch and the sync state from the health work: importing, healthy, or needs reconnecting. A workspace the rep sent from is shown as on. Turning a switch on shows "Importing" until recent history lands. Turning one off asks for a quick confirmation that new mail will stop arriving in that workspace and that existing CRM history stays. A rep in only one workspace sees a single switch that is already on.

## Done when

- [ ] A rep in two workspaces can switch their inbox on in both and new mail arrives in both CRMs without any further action.
- [ ] Switching a workspace on starts a recent-history import into that workspace and shows importing until it finishes.
- [ ] Switching a workspace off stops new mail arriving there and leaves the already imported history visible.
- [ ] Sending from a workspace that is switched off still works and leaves that workspace switched on afterwards.
- [ ] Disconnecting the inbox switches every workspace off and stops sync everywhere.
- [ ] A rep who leaves a workspace has that workspace switched off automatically.
- [ ] Only the inbox owner can change their own switches.
- [ ] Both Gmail and Outlook pass a live QA pass covering on, off, send from an off workspace, and disconnect.

## Open questions

* Should the same email thread appear in both workspaces when both are on? Recommended default: yes, each workspace keeps its own copy, the same way two separate connects would.
* Should turning a workspace off also cancel scheduled emails from that inbox in that workspace? Recommended default: no, scheduled sends still go out because sending does not depend on sync.
* Should the switch ship for Outlook at the same time as Gmail, given Microsoft live sync is not built yet? Recommended default: build the switch for both, but the Outlook side only becomes meaningful once Keep Microsoft 365 conversations up to date automatically lands.

## Expected outcome

A rep working in several CRMs decides once, in settings, which of them their inbox syncs into. Mail keeps arriving in every workspace they chose, sending never breaks, and nobody has to disconnect and reconnect to move an inbox around.

## Implementation context

Evidence, settled decisions, suggested direction and test seams: AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: Protect platform staff calendar details from normal users
relatedSnapshot.description:
Normal platform users could see closers' and other staff members' external event titles when those owners enabled sharing, exposing leads across client workspaces.

## Platform role boundary

“Client” means `user.role === 'user'`. Workspace owner/admin/member/client status does not override this restriction.

| Viewer | Calendar owner | External event titles |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Normal platform user | Another normal platform user | Visible only when the owner enables sharing |
| Normal platform user | Closer, admin, superadmin, customer success, or another non-normal role | Always masked as “External Event”, even with sharing enabled |
| Closer, admin, or customer success | Another user | Visible only when the owner enables sharing |
| Calendar owner | Themselves | Visible |
| Platform superadmin | Any user | Visible |

Masked events retain busy times. Missing or unknown owner roles do not qualify as normal-user sharing. Organization/calendar permissions and active workspace membership still limit accessible calendars.

## Impersonation

Calendar identity and role checks use the impersonated user. Staff impersonating a closer see the closer's own titles. A superadmin impersonating a normal platform user receives normal-user restrictions, even when the staff calendar owner has sharing enabled.

Sharing updates follow the existing current-session-user behavior. No calendar-specific impersonation restrictions or generic profile API changes are added. Existing session validation and the app-wide read-only mode for closers impersonating clients still apply.

## Workspace calls and booking attribution

Appointments belonging to the requested workspace retain their details, subject to existing calendar permissions. Other workspaces' appointments are not returned as that workspace's calls.

External booking tracking creates workspace-owned appointments from trusted workflow context. Preserve booking attribution, deduplication, and the response field allowlist. Do not infer workspace ownership from event titles. Staff-owned external bookings whose workspace is unknown remain masked from normal users until registered through the proper booking flow.

## Acceptance criteria

* Normal platform users cannot see staff external titles with sharing on or off, including when they are workspace owners/admins.
* A normal user's external titles require that owner's sharing opt-in for other non-superadmin viewers.
* Superadmins and calendar owners retain title visibility within their calendar access.
* Impersonation uses the impersonated user's role and ownership.
* Forged member IDs, deleted membership, or denied permissions cannot expand calendar access.
* Settings copy explains the sharing audience for normal users versus platform staff.
* No schema change or one-time closer preference reset is required; enforce the restriction when returning calendar data.

## Implementation and validation

fix(calendar): hide staff events from normal users (ENG-13599), base `main`, branch `codex/13599-cal-privacy`, head `86fae66161` (platform-role enforcement in `e80da49ec2`).

* 79 focused tests pass across the calendar-event and sharing-setting router suites.
* Twenty-three regression cases exposed titles under the previous rules and pass with the new platform-role boundary.
* Scoped Biome and diff checks pass.
* Full typecheck passes across all 13 packages. Existing declaration portability diagnostics remain non-blocking.
* Name 7 matrix and QA: `references/closer-calendar-privacy-rollout.md`.

## QA and deployment

Name 8 preview QA on `d413764431` verified toggle persistence and unchanged details for 278 workspace appointments. Preferences were restored and impersonation ended. The imported external account lacked safe OAuth credentials.

Live preview QA on final head `86fae66161` passed 206 checks on 9 September 2026, using one authorized Name 1 calendar connected to staff and normal-user profiles. All 50 viewer-role × calendar-owner-role × sharing-state combinations passed with real provider events and authenticated requests. Additional checks passed for own calendars, an actual superadmin session, both connections together, unknown owner roles, all four workspace roles, own-only/no calendar permissions, removed memberships, and workspace-owned booking fixtures. Superadmin/admin/customer-success impersonation followed the subject; the dedicated closer workspace flow followed the subject while retaining the existing app-wide read-only mutation guard. The 79 focused automated tests were rerun and passed. Browser QA verified role-specific setting copy and own/masked event displays.

All original preview roles, sharing flags, membership state, role assignments, and feature flags were restored and verified. Temporary booking, membership, role, and closer-assignment fixtures were removed. Both authorized Name 1 connections remain healthy with sharing off. No runtime code change or production deployment was made during QA. The real ads-provider booking workflow was not triggered; workspace attribution used preview appointment fixtures and existing automated deduplication tests.

Deployment enforces the normal-user restriction even if existing staff sharing flags are on; reverting the rule would restore stored sharing preferences.

## Source

Blaise reported that clients could see other clients' leads in closers' calendars. Mahmut clarified that clients are the normal platform `user.role`, that they must not see staff-owned external events regardless of sharing, and that impersonation must behave as the impersonated user.

Review follow-up: preserved server permission messages in the settings toggle and shortened the documentation reference. The earlier generic-profile concern is addressed by enforcing the platform-role boundary on calendar reads; no special profile-update or impersonation restriction was restored. All 13 package typechecks passed on the final head.

relatedSnapshot.title: Show a per-workspace Email sync switch in Email & Calendar settings
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A rep who belongs to more than one CRM workspace sees, under Email & Calendar settings, a switch for each workspace their connected inbox could sync into, and can turn any of them on or off themselves.

## Problem

Email & Calendar settings lists inboxes by person with no workspace information at all, and there is no way for a rep to say "sync this inbox into this workspace too." Let one connected mailbox hold an active binding in more than one workspace makes it possible underneath for a mailbox to be active in several workspaces, but nothing lets a rep see or control that yet.

## Proposed fix

Add a per-workspace "Email sync" switch to each connected inbox's card in settings, backed by the workspaces the rep currently belongs to and each one's binding state. Turning a switch on activates that workspace's binding and starts a recent-history import; turning it off deactivates that workspace's binding and stops new mail from arriving there, while leaving already-imported history in place.

## What's included

Included: extending the settings data to return, per connected inbox, every workspace the rep currently belongs to and whether that workspace's binding is on; the switch itself, following the existing toggle pattern already used in this settings page; the toggle mutation, restricted to the inbox owner and to workspaces they currently belong to; a fix to the sync-health lookup so it reports health per workspace instead of collapsing to one workspace once a mailbox has more than one active binding; and the "Importing" and off-switch confirmation copy described below.

Excluded: the underlying binding-model change (that is Let one connected mailbox hold an active binding in more than one workspace) and making Gmail's live mail notifications actually reach every switched-on workspace (that is Fan Gmail live sync out to every workspace an inbox is switched on in). Until that ticket lands, switching on a second workspace only gets a one-time history import, not ongoing new mail; this ticket does not need to hide that, since the sync-health state already shows importing versus healthy honestly.

## Blocked by

* Let one connected mailbox hold an active binding in more than one workspace

## How it should work

Each connected inbox's settings card lists every workspace the rep currently belongs to, each with its own switch reflecting whether that workspace's binding is active. A workspace the rep has sent from shows as already on. Turning a switch on activates that workspace's binding and shows "Importing" until the recent-history import finishes, then shows healthy. Turning a switch off asks a quick confirmation that new mail will stop arriving in that workspace and that the CRM history already imported there stays. A rep who belongs to only one workspace sees a single switch that is already on. A rep who is not a member of a workspace does not see a switch for it at all, and loses their switch for a workspace automatically if they leave it.

## Who can do what

Only the inbox owner can see or change the switches on their own inbox, and only for workspaces they are currently a member of. Workspace admins cannot turn another person's inbox on or off. The toggle mutation checks membership directly against the membership row, not session claims, so impersonation cannot bypass it.

## What the user sees

Under Email & Calendar, each connected inbox lists the rep's workspaces with a switch and a sync state: importing, healthy, or needs reconnecting. Turning a switch on shows "Importing" until recent history lands, then settles to healthy. Turning one off shows a quick confirmation, then the switch turns off and the workspace's existing history stays visible in CRM. A rep in only one workspace sees one switch that is already on and needs no attention.

## Done when

- [ ] A rep in two workspaces sees a separate switch for each, reflecting each workspace's real binding state.
- [ ] Turning a switch on activates that workspace's binding and shows "Importing" until the history import finishes.
- [ ] Turning a switch off deactivates that workspace's binding, asks for confirmation first, and leaves existing CRM history in that workspace visible.
- [ ] Sync-health state is reported correctly per workspace once a mailbox has more than one active binding, instead of only reporting one workspace's health.
- [ ] A non-owner or a person who is not a member of the workspace cannot toggle the switch.
- [ ] A rep in only one workspace sees a single switch that is already on.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

A rep working in several CRMs decides, in settings, which of them their inbox syncs into, sees accurate per-workspace status, and can change their mind at any time without disconnecting and reconnecting.

## Implementation context

* Context captured 17 September 2026 against origin/main at commit 30ad76855d.
* Data: `apps/web/lib/integrations/email/user-email-accounts.ts` and `apps/web/trpc/routers/integrations/email-calendar.ts` (`getAccountsAsCalendars`) currently query by the signed-in user only, with no membership or binding join. Add the join needed to return, per account, the rep's current workspace memberships and each one's binding state.
* Bug to fix along the way: the sync-health lookup that powers the health badges added in Show Gmail sync health and finish disconnect cleanup keys its result by account only. Once an account can have more than one active binding, that silently keeps only one workspace's health and drops the rest; key it by account and workspace instead.
* UI: `apps/web/components/user/email-calendar-accounts.tsx` already renders one card per connected account with a per-item switch pattern used for calendar conflict checking; add the per-workspace sync switch as a parallel section on the same card rather than restructuring the page.
* Toggle mutation should call the workspace-scoped ensure-active-binding and deactivate helpers built in Let one connected mailbox hold an active binding in more than one workspace, and should write an audit log entry per the repo's audit-logging convention for user-visible settings changes.
* Tests: add coverage for a non-owner and a non-member both being rejected by the toggle mutation, and for the settings query returning the right workspace-and-binding-state shape.

relatedSnapshot.title: Lock Outlook mailboxes to their connected workspace
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

For Outlook and Microsoft 365 connected mailboxes, make sure every sync, send, and disconnect action is checked against the one workspace that mailbox belongs to, so a mailbox can never sync or write into a workspace it is not bound to.

## Problem

Sync and send already require the acting person to be a member of the target workspace (ENG-12570, shipped). But a person who belongs to more than one workspace can still have an Outlook mailbox's sync attributed to the wrong one of their workspaces, because nothing pins a specific mailbox to a specific workspace. This same ambiguity currently makes a calendar-booking lookup give up entirely (skip matching instead of resolving correctly) whenever a person's memberships span more than one workspace.

## Proposed fix

When someone connects an Outlook mailbox, record which workspace they connected it to, using the workspace already selected as part of that Microsoft sign-in. From then on, every Outlook sync job, webhook-triggered lookup, and disconnect action checks against that one recorded workspace instead of inferring it live from the person's current memberships.

## What's included

* Persist the workspace binding (from the mailbox-binding foundation ticket, linked below) when an Outlook mailbox is connected.
* Disconnecting an Outlook mailbox deactivates its binding first, then cleans up with Microsoft, so nothing can write using a disconnected mailbox even if the cleanup step fails partway through.
* Outlook sync jobs and the calendar-booking lookup check the mailbox's bound workspace and generation instead of scanning the connecting person's current memberships.
* Reauthorizing (reconnecting) an Outlook mailbox never silently moves it to a different workspace.
* Not included: Gmail/Name 1 mailboxes (separate ticket).

## Blocked by

* The mailbox-binding foundation ticket (linked below): needs the binding record to exist before anything can write to or read from it.

## How it should work

Connecting an Outlook mailbox binds it to the workspace it was connected from. Every later Outlook sync or webhook-triggered lookup for that mailbox reads that one binding rather than checking which workspaces the owner currently belongs to. If the owner loses access to that workspace, future syncs and sends for that mailbox stop. Disconnecting immediately blocks any further writes from that mailbox, even if Microsoft's own cleanup step fails partway through.

## Who can do what

Same as today: only the mailbox's owner can connect or disconnect it. This ticket adds no new sharing or visibility.

## What the user sees

No visible UI change. The practical effect is that an Outlook mailbox's synced emails and calendar events reliably land in the one workspace it is connected to, including for people who belong to several workspaces.

## Done when

- [ ] An Outlook mailbox cannot have two active workspace bindings at once.
- [ ] An Outlook sync or write attempt against a workspace the mailbox is not bound to fails.
- [ ] Disconnecting an Outlook mailbox blocks further writes even if the Microsoft-side cleanup step fails.
- [ ] Reconnecting an Outlook mailbox to the same workspace keeps the same binding and just advances it; it never silently moves the mailbox to a different workspace.
- [ ] The calendar-booking lookup that currently gives up when a person's memberships span multiple workspaces now resolves correctly using the mailbox's bound workspace.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Outlook-connected mailboxes always sync into, and can only be used from, the one workspace they were connected to.

## Implementation context

Detailed file:line evidence and technical decisions: AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: Prove workspace isolation end to end and prepare the Fin v1 pilot
relatedSnapshot.description:
Before expanding Fin beyond the current Preview audience, demonstrate that the complete customer → Fin → Foreman → Fin path preserves investigation quality and workspace access boundaries.

## Test matrix

* Two users in separate workspaces; one user in two authorized workspaces; concurrent tabs and conversations; workspace switch during an active run.
* Existing member roles and private/team resources, changed or revoked membership, inactive organizations, anonymous/unverified users and mismatched Intercom apps.
* Forged workspace/resource IDs, swapped or expired run references, and direct/indirect instructions attempting to broaden access.
* Every supported evidence provider, including raw/helper entry points and delegated work. Confirm authorized evidence is useful and unauthorized data never reaches the model or customer.
* Retry versus intentional new investigation, out-of-order callbacks, delayed completion beyond ten minutes, provider/callback failure, missed callback and authorized result recovery.
* Messenger panel close, page reload and temporary disconnect. Only promise off-page/offline updates after that specific behavior is verified.
* Fin's natural clarification and final answer fidelity; internal Slack receipt and terminal update.
* A Fin-triggered investigation that warrants follow-up creates a correctly routed Name 18 ticket with authorized evidence, and Fin tells the originating customer after confirmed creation while Fin owns communication; after human takeover the confirmed result goes to Slack without an automated customer reply. Include an existing ticket, no ticket needed, failed or uncertain creation, retried delivery and no duplicate tickets. Ensure internal ticket content and other customers' cases cannot leak through the reply.
* Customer-initiated status follow-ups in the original conversation and a fresh Fin chat after the investigation's one-hour window. Include several matching cases, missing/forged references, revoked case access, shared/master-ticket updates, no new information and unavailable Name 18. Verify accurate customer-safe current updates, without duplicate tickets, restarted investigations or automatic ticket mutations.
* Regression coverage for existing internal Foreman and scheduled-support access without enabling uncontrolled scheduled tests.

## Additional agreed interaction acceptance (2026-09-14)

* One active investigation per conversation; retries and follow-up messages do not duplicate it. Separate conversations can run independently. After completion, an open ticket does not prevent another investigation.
* Preserve the one-hour webhook wait with no new 20-minute cutoff. Additional deadline-triggered stop, restart or handoff behavior is deferred and is not a new v1 acceptance gate.
* One progress update at ten minutes while still running and Fin owns communication; no recurring five-minute updates.
* A human customer-facing reply suppresses subsequent automated customer messages, including progress, ticket confirmations and final results. Test takeover before progress and near completion. Investigation continues and updates/results reach the associated Slack thread.
* Teammates can answer questions and direct the associated investigation through Slack without starting another investigation or changing its authorized scope.
* "Check ticket status" invokes the independent authorized status workflow, including during an active investigation. It creates neither an investigation nor a ticket.
* "I found a bug" invokes investigation with the retained optional Jam recording step after symptoms and before start. Test skip and late Jam evidence attached to the same case without a duplicate run.
* Natural-language reports and status requests reach the same workflows without requiring quick-message buttons.

## Release preparation

Record the exact Preview deployment SHA, connector identities, Executor bindings, audience and Procedure configuration used for acceptance. Reconcile stale Preview documentation with the current workspace context and one-hour wait.

Prepare the smallest promotion/configuration changes needed from the preview-gated endpoint, an explicit pilot audience, and a rollback that disables the new entry without disrupting established workflows. Exclude experimental customer write connectors and credentials. Keep production changes and audience expansion gated on explicit rollout approval.

## Acceptance

Attach observed evidence for positive and negative cases and list any unresolved coverage or provider-authentication gaps. Build/discovery alone is not acceptance. Run representative Fin-originated investigations through completion and compare source findings with the final customer reply. For a ticket-producing case, attach the created Name 18 ticket and the matching Fin confirmation; verify correct workspace/conversation association.

All implementation children must meet their own acceptance criteria before the pilot is marked ready. Internal Name 18 ticket filing, its Fin confirmation and later customer-initiated ticket follow-ups are required v1 acceptance. Product-changing customer actions, browser automation and a broader rollout remain outside this ticket.

## Preview regression observation — 2026-09-14

During ENG-13763 testing, a read-only request in #foreman-preview used the ordinary Slack path. The human-browser request reached the PR132 deployment, read the repository and launched two native reviewers; its final review has now arrived. It found a deployment-wide Executor toolkit switch affecting ordinary Slack, addressed in PR132 commit 3fd2b1b. Its separate critic pass was not completed.

A stop was requested for a separate duplicate request with a normal `<mention> Preview stop` message. Vercel recorded an `app_mention handler failed` error: `Timed out waiting for session "wrun_41M2GKG1QM0GZ7MDCRRTPFQYG3" to release its command inbox.` The stop targeted the correct existing session. HTTP 200 was only webhook acknowledgement; no `Stop requested.` reply appeared. Later Vercel logs showed the original turn cancelled at 18:55:31.04 UTC, about 117 seconds after the stop request. A normal follow-up, “Which PR were we looking at? Just the link please,” then started fresh session `wrun_41M2GMKGTN0GXDY7KBZB1B7KRD` at 18:59:21 UTC and returned the correct PR link. Eventual cancellation and fresh-session continuation worked; the delayed cancellation and missing stop acknowledgement remain unresolved. This is separate from the successful Fin workspace checks.

Evidence: duplicate request and stop; stop message `1789412013.311499`, Vercel request at 18:53:33.83 UTC, error ID `<uuid>`. The original run used runtime `918c6d50`; the stop handler used `8e92a5f5` (test/docs-only follow-up, unchanged runtime source). Existing Eve reset waits up to 30 seconds for inbox release; its timeout does not establish that the run was retired. Resolve and repeat this check before internal Slack regression acceptance is complete.

## Cancellation investigation update — 2026-09-14

Treat the delayed stop as an existing Foreman regression blocking the current ENG-13763 acceptance, not a behavior deferred to the Fin pilot. Yesterday's genuine Slack stop cancelled active work in about four seconds and posted confirmation in five. Today's failed run stayed in a Vercel invocation until its 800-second hard timeout at 18:54:07.410 UTC; cancellation then settled on the retried step at 18:55:31.040. The public reset's 30-second wait had already failed, so its acknowledgement was never sent. Slack cancellation source, locked Eve 0.54.2 dependencies and ordinary Slack model cancellation-signal forwarding are unchanged; the exact reason for delayed runtime control remains unproven. Name 19 evidence and supported API limits are in Foreman .github/EVE-PROPOSALS.md.

A second genuine Slack stop at 19:27:10.114 UTC returned “Stop requested.” at 19:27:36.714, approximately 26.6 seconds later. This proves that reset can complete but does not establish a return to yesterday's latency or erase the first failure. Repeat test thread. No cancellation workaround or Production change has been shipped.

relatedSnapshot.title: Lock Gmail mailboxes to their connected workspace
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

For Gmail-connected mailboxes, make sure every sync, send, and disconnect action is checked against the one workspace that mailbox belongs to, so a mailbox can never sync or write into a workspace it is not bound to.

## Problem

Sync and send already require the acting person to be a member of the target workspace (ENG-12570, shipped). But a person who belongs to more than one workspace can still have a Gmail mailbox's sync attributed to the wrong one of their workspaces, because nothing pins a specific mailbox to a specific workspace. This same ambiguity currently makes a calendar-booking lookup give up entirely (skip matching instead of resolving correctly) whenever a person's memberships span more than one workspace.

## Proposed fix

When someone connects a Gmail mailbox, record which workspace they connected it to, using the workspace already selected as part of that Name 1 sign-in. From then on, every Gmail sync job, webhook-triggered lookup, and disconnect action checks against that one recorded workspace instead of inferring it live from the person's current memberships.

## What's included

* Persist the workspace binding (from the mailbox-binding foundation ticket, linked below) when a Gmail mailbox is connected.
* Disconnecting a Gmail mailbox deactivates its binding first, then cleans up with Name 1, so nothing can write using a disconnected mailbox even if the cleanup step fails partway through.
* Gmail sync jobs and the calendar-booking lookup check the mailbox's bound workspace and generation instead of scanning the connecting person's current memberships.
* Reauthorizing (reconnecting) a Gmail mailbox never silently moves it to a different workspace.
* Not included: Outlook/Microsoft 365 mailboxes (separate ticket).

## Blocked by

* The mailbox-binding foundation ticket (linked below): needs the binding record to exist before anything can write to or read from it.

## How it should work

Connecting a Gmail mailbox binds it to the workspace it was connected from. Every later Gmail sync or webhook-triggered lookup for that mailbox reads that one binding rather than checking which workspaces the owner currently belongs to. If the owner loses access to that workspace, future syncs and sends for that mailbox stop. Disconnecting immediately blocks any further writes from that mailbox, even if Name 1's own cleanup step fails partway through.

## Who can do what

Same as today: only the mailbox's owner can connect or disconnect it. This ticket adds no new sharing or visibility.

## What the user sees

No visible UI change. The practical effect is that a Gmail mailbox's synced emails and calendar events reliably land in the one workspace it is connected to, including for people who belong to several workspaces.

## Done when

- [ ] A Gmail mailbox cannot have two active workspace bindings at once.
- [ ] A Gmail sync or write attempt against a workspace the mailbox is not bound to fails.
- [ ] Disconnecting a Gmail mailbox blocks further writes even if the Google-side cleanup step fails.
- [ ] Reconnecting a Gmail mailbox to the same workspace keeps the same binding and just advances it; it never silently moves the mailbox to a different workspace.
- [ ] The calendar-booking lookup that currently gives up when a person's memberships span multiple workspaces now resolves correctly using the mailbox's bound workspace.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Gmail-connected mailboxes always sync into, and can only be used from, the one workspace they were connected to.

## Implementation context

Detailed file:line evidence and technical decisions: AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: Workspace email/salesperson changes still bleed across workspaces
relatedSnapshot.description:
A customer reports that campaign/growth plan sending and workspace profile details (name/email) are still not isolated between their workspace and a client workspace.

They report:

* Changing assigned salesperson/calendar/email in one workspace affects the other.
* Their workspace still shows the client’s name/email; expected to show Name 14 and use `<email>` / `<email>`.
* Growth plan activity in their workspace appears to still route through the client’s email even after a fix was released.

The troubleshooting path included inviting `<email>` to the relevant workspace(s). The customer says the client attempted to accept the invitation but was prompted for a password that was reported as incorrect, and the invitation/activation did not reliably reflect in the app.

relatedSnapshot.title: Email/calendar connections bleed across workspaces
relatedSnapshot.description:
user: <email>

Workspace profile settings and connected email/calendar appear to sync across two workspaces under the same user account.

Reported behavior:

* Connecting/re-authenticating email + calendar in one workspace causes the other workspace to show the same email/calendar.
* Changing the profile name/email in one workspace can also reflect in the other.
* Campaign bookings/notifications can end up on the client’s email/calendar, sometimes showing the reporter’s name with the client’s email.
* Attempting to set the client workspace profile email to the client email can error with: `User already exists. Use another email`.

Example emails involved:

* Client: <email> (account under Name 21)
